examples.problem: Suppose we wish to find a root of the function $f(x)=e^x-x^3-3$ in the interval $[4,6].$ Calculate the second iteration of the Newton-Raphson process starting from the point $x_0 = 5.$ Round your answer to three decimal places.
examples.worked_solution:
The formula for the Newton-Raphson method is

$$
x_{n+1} = x_n - \dfrac{f(x_n)}{f'(x_n)}
$$

where $f'(x_n)$ is the derivative of $f(x)$ evaluated at $x_n.$

In our case, we have

$$
f'(x) = (e^x-x^3-3)' = e^x-3x^2.
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{n+1} & ={x}_{n}-\frac{{e}^{{x}_{n}}-{x}_{n}^{3}-3}{{e}^{{x}_{n}}-3{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Starting with $x_0 = 5,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={x}_{0}-\frac{{e}^{{x}_{0}}-{x}_{0}^{3}-3}{{e}^{{x}_{0}}-3{x}_{0}^{2}} \\  & =5-\frac{{e}^{5}-{5}^{3}-3}{{e}^{5}-3(5)^{2}} \\  & =4.721\,941…\end{aligned}
$$

For the second iteration, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & ={x}_{1}-\frac{{e}^{{x}_{1}}-{x}_{1}^{3}-3}{{e}^{{x}_{1}}-3{x}_{1}^{2}} \\  & =(4.721\,941…)-\frac{{e}^{4.721\,941…}-(4.721\,941…)^{3}-3}{{e}^{4.721\,941…}-3(4.721\,941…)^{2}} \\  & ≈4.632,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places.

feedback.worked_solution:
The formula for the Newton-Raphson method is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-\frac{f({x}_{n})}{{f}^{′}({x}_{n})}
$$

where ${f}^{′}({x}_{n})$ is the derivative of $f(x)$ evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)={(\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\frac{x}{10})}^{′}=\operatorname{cos}⁡x-\frac{1}{10}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{n+1} & ={x}_{n}-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡{x}_{n}-\frac{{x}_{n}}{10}}{\operatorname{cos}⁡{x}_{n}-\frac{1}{10}} \\  & ={x}_{n}-\frac{10\operatorname{sin}⁡{x}_{n}-{x}_{n}}{10\operatorname{cos}⁡{x}_{n}-1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Starting with ${x}_{0}=7,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={x}_{0}-\frac{10\operatorname{sin}⁡{x}_{0}-{x}_{0}}{10\operatorname{cos}⁡{x}_{0}-1} \\  & =7-\frac{10\operatorname{sin}⁡(7)-7}{10\operatorname{cos}⁡(7)-1} \\  & ≈7.066,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places.
